entities.name: Cristoforo Landino
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cristoforo Landino was a prominent Italian humanist and polymath of the Florentine Renaissance. He played a crucial role in shaping the intellectual and artistic landscape of 15th-century Italy, collaborating with key figures such as Lorenzo de' Medici and Leon Battista Alberti.

Born around 1424, Landino moved to Florence at a young age and became increasingly involved in the city's cultural and political circles. He was a prolific writer and poet, producing works on literature, philosophy, and history that drew heavily from classical sources.

Landino's literary legacy extends beyond his own writings, as he helped to establish the Tuscan dialect as the standard for Italian literature. His influence can also be seen in the work of later Renaissance writers, such as Machiavelli and Boccaccio.

Today, Cristoforo Landino is remembered as a key figure in the evolution of the Italian language and culture, marking an important turning point in the development of humanism and Renaissance thought.
